name: Petmania
description: Product design for an app connecting pet owners in urban neighborhoods.

text: Made in collaboration with two Parsons graduates, Petmania addresses a real gap in urban life. There's no good way for pet owners to connect with nearby pet owners, especially in cities like New York where interactions with neighbors are rare. Pets need companionship, owners need trusted people who can pet sit, and neighborhoods lack a system for making those connections happen.
The design process started with proto-personas to map out the target audience and understand their daily frustrations.
Paper sketches served as rapid prototypes. Common threads emerged across the team's ideas, including personalized filters for types of pets and a photo sharing layer that doubles as a social catalog.
Ten pages were designed in Figma based on user testing from the lo-fi prototype, starting with wireframes to establish the information architecture.
A user flow mapped the complete journey through the app, from onboarding to connecting with nearby owners.

For the visual identity, a paw became the logo. The brand needed to feel trustworthy, warm, and fun. After several iterations, the team landed on a warm aqua and gold palette. The colors evoke beach tones and reflect the app's themes of outdoor connection and play.
